Review found that a concrete arms value passed to identity<T>(T)->T works in ordinary Choice but fails in a generated-record spread because native shape discovery insists on explicit generic arguments. The generated field list is needed before the graph can be sealed; the later sealed checker remains responsible for valid expressions, effects and arm result/error compatibility. Existing inference walks nominal/array/callable templates transactionally, refuses conflicting bindings and reports unresolved parameters, but only accepts sealed types. Consider reusing the same equality walker behind a private builder-graph evidence check: infer from actual arguments and method receiver, compare interned node identity, retain ambiguity/conflict/cycle rejection, and keep the exported solver sealed-only. Contrast premature graph sealing with preserving an explicit-only generated-spread rule. Evaluate correctness of this bounded shape discovery while requiring ordinary final checking and forbidding type-search fallback.
